stories.title: Researchers unveil Wave Forcing for real-time streaming video generation
stories.summary: A new paper proposes Wave Forcing, a method that co-designs generation, training, and execution to stream long videos in real time without the quality loss or camera drift of prior autoregressive approaches.
stories.more: Existing chunk-wise autoregressive video models require two forward passes per step even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts tend to degrade quality and cause camera drift. Wave Forcing addresses this by co-designing generation, training, and execution together, aiming for continuous video output with consistent appearance and natural motion. The paper targets real-time, long-form video generation rather than short clips. The excerpt does not give details on model size, benchmarks, or release plans.

stories.title: Study traces how fine-tuning data quietly erodes LLM safety
stories.summary: Researchers introduce SimpleLoRIF, a method that flags fine-tuning examples whose gradients align with unsafe behavior, even when the training data looks harmless and evades standard content filters.
stories.more: The paper shows that fine-tuning large language models on instruction data can erode safety without any individual example appearing harmful, letting the degradation slip past standard content filters. SimpleLoRIF is a scalable gradient-embedding method that traces safety loss back to specific training examples by checking whether their gradients align with unsafe behavior. It simplifies an existing low-rank attribution technique and restricts backpropagation to the final few transformer layers to make this tractable. The excerpt does not give quantitative results or say which models were tested.

items.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
items.excerpt: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on instruction data can quietly erode their safety, even when no training example looks harmful. Because this safety-degrading data looks benign, standard content filters struggle to catch it. We tackle this problem by developing SimpleLoRIF, a scalable gradient embedding method that identifies fine-tuning examples whose gradients align with unsafe behavior. stories.title: OSINT video shows background plane noise can reveal a recording's exact location
stories.summary: Simon Willison highlighted an OSINT video by Colsto showing how faint background aircraft noise in a recording can be used to pinpoint its exact location via Doppler and ADS-B data.
stories.more: The technique uses near-imperceptible background plane noise captured in a video's soundtrack. By measuring the Doppler curve of that noise and cross-referencing it against ADS-B flight-tracking data, the method can determine a plane's speed, distance, and timing gaps precisely enough to locate where the video was recorded. Willison shared the video via Lobste.rs, tagging it under privacy and YouTube.
